q: The Official Language Implementation Committee (Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) constituted in a Central Government office is chaired by:

options.B: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.C: The nominee of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee
options.D: The senior-most clerk of the office

e: The Official Language Implementation Committee (Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) in a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office.

q: Meetings of the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office are normally held:
e: Meetings of the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office are normally held every quarter.

q: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is constituted in a town or city which has:

options.B: Ten or more Central Government offices

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is constituted in a town or city having ten or more Central Government offices.

q: Meetings of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) are normally held:
e: Meetings of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee are normally held twice a year.

q: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee (Kendriya Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is chaired by:

options.A: The Secretary, Department of Official Language

e: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee (Kendriya Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.

q: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry is chaired by:

options.B: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.C: The Minister in charge of the Ministry
options.D: The senior-most Member of Parliament associated with the Ministry

e: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of the Ministry.

q: The Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the year:
e: The Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the year 1975.

q: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) was set up in the year:
e: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) was set up in the year 1961.

q: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) functions under the:
e: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Ministry of Education.

q: The main function of the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) is:

options.A: To evolve and define scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and to publish glossaries and definitional dictionaries
options.B: To conduct Hindi examinations for Central Government employees
options.C: To inspect Central Government offices for the use of Hindi
options.D: To translate judgments of the Supreme Court and High Courts

e: The main function of the CSTT is to evolve and define scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and to publish glossaries and definitional dictionaries.

q: The Central Hindi Directorate (Kendriya Hindi Nideshalaya) was established in the year:
e: The Central Hindi Directorate (Kendriya Hindi Nideshalaya) was established in the year 1960.

q: The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, meant for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by:
e: The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.

q: The in-service training of Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is organised by:

options.A: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi
options.D: The Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration

e: In-service training of Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is organised by the Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi.

q: Hindi workshops (Hindi Karyashala) are organised in Central Government offices primarily to:

options.A: Teach Hindi literature to the staff
options.B: Prepare the staff only for the Pragya examination
options.C: Give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi

e: Hindi workshops (Hindi Karyashala) are organised to give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.

q: The first World Hindi Conference (Vishwa Hindi Sammelan) was held in the year 1975 at:
e: The first World Hindi Conference (Vishwa Hindi Sammelan) was held in the year 1975 at Nagpur.

q: The three-language formula for school education was adopted as a part of the:
e: The three-language formula for school education was adopted as a part of the National Policy on Education, 1968.

q: Under the three-language formula, the three languages to be studied in the Hindi-speaking States are:

options.B: Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably one of the southern languages

e: Under the three-language formula, the Hindi-speaking States are to study Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably one of the southern languages.

q: A lumpsum award under the incentive schemes relating to the Hindi examinations is admissible to an employee who passes the prescribed examination:

options.A: After completing the full-time training course
options.B: Only on securing full marks in the examination
options.C: Through his own efforts (self-study), without undergoing the prescribed training

e: A lumpsum award is admissible to an employee who passes the prescribed Hindi examination through his own efforts, that is, by self-study without undergoing the prescribed training.

q: The training imparted to Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is:

options.A: On payment of a fee by the employee and outside office hours
options.B: Free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty
options.D: Imparted only while the employee is on casual leave

e: Training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is imparted free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty.

q: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded to:

options.A: Individual authors for original book writing in Hindi
options.B: The best Hindi film of the year
options.C: The best railway station of the year
options.D: Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy

e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is awarded to Ministries and Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy.

q: A licence (permit) is to be issued by a Central Government office. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, such a licence or permit is required to be issued in:

options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Licences and permits are among the documents specified in Section 3(3), so a licence or permit must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: An administrative report of a Central Government office is to be laid before both Houses of Parliament. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the report is required to be issued in:

options.D: English, with a Hindi summary attached at the end

e: An administrative report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament is a Section 3(3) document and must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: An employee records his noting on a file in Hindi. His superior officer asks him to also furnish an English translation of the noting. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976:

options.A: The employee must furnish the translation on demand
options.B: The employee cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting in the other language
options.C: Only a gazetted officer can be asked for such a translation
options.D: The translation has to be prepared by the Hindi Translator at the employee's cost

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting or drafting in the other language.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the headings of registers used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the headings of registers used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English, that is, bilingually.

q: A newly opened branch of a Central Government office gets its rubber stamps prepared in English only. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, the rubber stamps used in the office should be prepared:

options.A: In English only, as stamps are internal stationery
options.B: In bilingual form, i.e., in Hindi and English

e: Rubber stamps used in Central Government offices should be prepared in bilingual form, that is, in Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office wishes to release an advertisement in newspapers. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the advertisement should be released:

options.A: In Hindi and English (bilingual), i.e., in both Hindi and English newspapers
options.B: In English newspapers only, as advertisements are meant for the educated public
options.C: Only in the regional language newspaper of the area
options.D: Only in Hindi newspapers during Hindi Pakhwada and in English newspapers otherwise

e: In accordance with the Official Language Policy, an advertisement of a Central Government office should be released in Hindi and English newspapers, that is, bilingually.

q: A Hindi-speaking citizen telephones a Central Government office and begins the conversation in Hindi. The official attending the call should, as far as possible, reply to him:

options.A: In English only, telephone replies being official communications
options.B: Only after transferring the call to the Hindi Cell
options.C: In the regional language of the office

e: When a Hindi-speaking citizen begins a telephone conversation in Hindi, the official attending the call should, as far as possible, reply to him in Hindi.

q: For doing Hindi work on computers in Central Government offices, the font/encoding that should be used, so that the document can be read and exchanged on any computer system, is:

options.B: The Kruti Dev font, which is system-specific
options.C: Any ornamental English font with Hindi characters pasted as pictures
options.D: Hand-written text scanned and pasted into the document

e: For Hindi work on computers, a Unicode-compliant font such as Mangal should be used so that the document can be read and exchanged on any computer system.

q: The standard keyboard layout prescribed for Hindi (Devanagari) typing on computers, as per the Bureau of Indian Standards standard adopted for the purpose, is:

options.B: A phonetic layout designed by each office for itself
options.D: The English QWERTY layout with stickers pasted on the keys

e: The standard keyboard layout prescribed for Hindi (Devanagari) typing on computers, as per the Bureau of Indian Standards, is InScript.

q: Software packages procured for use in Central Government offices are required to have the facility of working:

options.A: In English only, Hindi work being done on typewriters
options.B: In Hindi as well, i.e., bilingual (Hindi-English) capability
options.C: Only in the regional language of the State of posting
options.D: In Hindi only, with no provision for English

e: Software packages procured for Central Government offices are required to have bilingual capability, that is, the facility of working in Hindi as well as English.

q: The progress made in the use of Hindi in a Central Government office is reported through the Quarterly Progress Report (Traimasik Pragati Report), which the office is required to send:

options.A: Only once, at the time the office is opened
options.B: Only when the Department of Official Language specifically demands it
options.D: Once in five years, along with the office inspection

e: The Quarterly Progress Report (Traimasik Pragati Report) on the progress of Hindi use is required to be sent by the office every quarter.

q: Before visiting a Central Government office for inspection, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language obtains detailed information about the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that office through:

options.A: A prescribed questionnaire (Prashnavali) filled in by the office
options.B: A secret enquiry conducted by the local police
options.C: The annual confidential reports of the staff
options.D: The audit report of the office for the previous year

e: Before inspecting an office, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language obtains detailed information about implementation of the Official Language Policy through a prescribed questionnaire (Prashnavali) filled in by the office.

q: Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the duty of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is to:

options.A: Conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations every year
options.B: Translate all Central Government codes and manuals into Hindi
options.C: Impose penalties on offices which do not use Hindi
options.D: Review the progress made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and submit a report to the President, with recommendations

e: Under Section 4, the duty of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is to review the progress made in the use of Hindi for official purposes of the Union and to submit a report to the President with recommendations.

q: The Hindi Teaching Scheme (Hindi Shikshan Yojana) for Central Government employees is administered by:

options.B: The Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs

e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme (Hindi Shikshan Yojana) for Central Government employees is administered by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is imparted to employees posted all over the country mainly through:

options.A: A single training centre located at Agra
options.B: Correspondence lessons only, there being no training centres
options.C: The Central Hindi Training Institute at New Delhi and its sub-offices located in various parts of the country
options.D: The universities of the States in which the employees are posted

e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is imparted mainly through the Central Hindi Training Institute at New Delhi and its sub-offices located in various parts of the country.

q: The provisions of Article 343 of the Constitution (Hindi in Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union) came into operation on:

options.B: 26th January, 1950, with the commencement of the Constitution

e: The provisions of Article 343 came into operation on 26 January 1950, with the commencement of the Constitution.

q: World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas) is observed every year on:
e: World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas) is observed every year on 10 January, distinct from Hindi Diwas which falls on 14 September.

q: The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission), appointed in 1955, submitted its report to the President in the year:
e: The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission), appointed in 1955, submitted its report to the President in the year 1956.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Memorandum" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Memorandum" is "Gyapan".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Circular" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Circular" is "Paripatra".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Reminder" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Reminder" is "Anusmarak".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Notification" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Notification" is "Adhisuchna".

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Increment" (in pay) is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of "Increment" in pay is "Vetan Vriddhi", signifying a periodic rise in pay.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Sanction" (of expenditure) is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of "Sanction" of expenditure is "Swikriti", meaning formal approval accorded by the competent authority.

q: The "Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali" (Comprehensive Glossary of Administrative Terms), which is the standard reference for Hindi equivalents of administrative terms, is published by:

options.D: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology

e: The Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali (Comprehensive Glossary of Administrative Terms) is published by the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology.

q: The standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani), adopted for official use, was prepared by:
e: The standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani), adopted for official use, was prepared by the Central Hindi Directorate.

q: The Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts is prepared by:

options.A: The Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts is prepared by the Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice.

q: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for:

options.A: The best implementation of Official Language Policy by a Zonal Railway
options.B: The best Hindi film of the year
options.C: Original book writing in Hindi (on specified subjects)
options.D: The best Hindi essay written during Hindi Pakhwada

e: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects.

q: Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi run by the Department of Official Language, the cash awards admissible to an employee are assessed mainly on the basis of:

options.A: His marks in the Pragya examination
options.B: The number of files disposed of by him in a year
options.C: The length of his service in Region 'A'
options.D: The number of words of noting and drafting written by him in Hindi during the year

e: Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, cash awards are assessed mainly on the number of words of noting and drafting written by the employee in Hindi during the year.

q: Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, different percentage targets for Hindi correspondence are prescribed for Regions 'A', 'B' and 'C' because:

options.A: The targets are drawn by lottery every year
options.B: The targets are graded according to the linguistic environment of the region — highest for Region 'A' and lowest for Region 'C'
options.C: Region 'C' offices are exempt from all targets
options.D: The same target applies to all regions and the regions are only for postal purposes

e: Annual Programme targets for Hindi correspondence are graded according to the linguistic environment of the region, being highest for Region A and lowest for Region C.

q: Announcements for the guidance of passengers at railway stations are made in:

options.A: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English
options.C: English and the regional language only

e: Station announcements must reach every passenger, so they are made in three languages: the regional language of the area, Hindi and English.

q: The reservation and cancellation requisition forms supplied to passengers at railway reservation offices are printed in:
e: Forms meant for the travelling public, such as reservation and cancellation requisition forms, are printed bilingually in Hindi and English for the convenience of passengers.

q: During Hindi Pakhwada, Central Government offices and Railways normally organise, among other things:

options.A: Only a formal inaugural function on the first day
options.B: Compulsory written Hindi examination for all staff
options.C: Transfer of all non-Hindi knowing staff to Region 'C'
options.D: Hindi essay, noting-and-drafting, elocution and Hindi typing competitions, Hindi workshops and related programmes

e: Hindi Pakhwada is an awareness fortnight; offices mark it with Hindi essay, noting-and-drafting, elocution and Hindi typing competitions, Hindi workshops and similar programmes to promote the use of Hindi.

q: Correspondence of a Central Government office with a foreign Government, or with the embassy of a foreign country in India, is conducted in:

options.C: Hindi and English both, as in Section 3(3) documents
options.D: The official language of that foreign country

e: Correspondence with foreign Governments and their embassies in India is external communication and is conducted in English, the internationally understood language, not under the bilingual Section 3(3) requirement.

q: A State Government office located in Region 'A' ordinarily corresponds with Central Government offices in:

options.C: The regional language through the Governor's Secretariat
options.D: Both Hindi and English, every letter being issued in two copies

e: Region 'A' consists of Hindi-speaking States where Hindi is the official language and is widely understood, so a State Government office there ordinarily corresponds with Central Government offices in Hindi.

q: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of the Ministry of Railways functions mainly to:

options.A: Conduct the Hindi examinations of railway employees
options.B: Translate all railway codes and manuals into Hindi
options.C: Advise the Ministry on matters relating to the progressive use of Hindi and the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.D: Inspect railway stations and impose penalties for non-use of Hindi

e: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti is an advisory body; it advises the Ministry of Railways on the progressive use of Hindi and the implementation of the Official Language Policy.

q: "Rajbhasha Bharati", the quarterly journal devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by:
e: "Rajbhasha Bharati" is the quarterly journal of the Department of Official Language, the nodal department for implementing the Official Language Policy of the Union.

q: The Official Language Policy of the Union is implemented in Central Government offices mainly through:

options.A: Compulsion and penal action against employees who do not know Hindi
options.B: Persuasion, encouragement and incentives, and not through compulsion
options.C: Stoppage of increments of employees who do not pass Pragya
options.D: Making Hindi the sole medium of all office work from a fixed date

e: The Official Language Policy is implemented through persuasion, encouragement and incentives; it does not rest on compulsion or penal action against employees who do not know Hindi.

q: The classification of States into Region 'A', Region 'B' and Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules is based mainly on:

options.A: The extent to which Hindi is the official language of the State and is widely spoken and understood there
options.B: The geographical size of the State
options.C: The number of Central Government offices located in the State
options.D: The literacy rate of the State

e: The region classification follows the position of Hindi in the State: States where Hindi is the official language and is widely spoken and understood form Region 'A', with Regions 'B' and 'C' graded below it.

q: A Hindi-speaking passenger approaches the enquiry counter of a railway station with a query. The railway staff at the counter should, as far as possible, attend to him:

options.A: Only in English, enquiries being official work
options.B: After calling an interpreter from the Rajbhasha section
options.D: Only in the regional language of the State

e: Public service at a counter should be rendered in the language the passenger understands, so a Hindi-speaking passenger is to be attended to in Hindi as far as possible.

q: For working out the percentage of Hindi correspondence of an office in the Quarterly Progress Report, letters are counted as Hindi correspondence only when they are:

options.A: Signed by an officer who knows Hindi
options.B: Typed on a computer in the Kruti Dev font
options.C: Addressed to offices located in Region 'A'
options.D: Originally written and issued in Hindi; an English draft merely translated into Hindi is not counted as Hindi correspondence

e: For the Quarterly Progress Report, only letters originally written and issued in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; an English draft merely translated into Hindi is not counted.

q: The standard (level) of the Pragya course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the standard of Hindi of:
e: Pragya is the final course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme, and its standard broadly corresponds to the Matriculation (Class X) standard of Hindi.

q: At the commencement of the Constitution, the number of languages included in the Eighth Schedule was:
e: At the commencement of the Constitution in 1950, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages; later amendments raised the number to the present 22.

q: The language Sindhi was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by:
e: Sindhi was included in the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967, raising the total number of scheduled languages from 14 to 15.

q: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution in the year 1992 by:
e: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule in 1992 by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, taking the total to 18 languages.

q: Chapter II of Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 345 to 347) is titled:

options.C: Language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts

e: Chapter II of Part XVII (Articles 345 to 347) deals with the official languages of the States, and is therefore titled "Regional Languages".

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter IV of Part XVII of the Constitution is titled "Special Directives".
2. Article 351 directs Hindi to draw its vocabulary primarily from English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: Chapter IV of Part XVII (Articles 350 to 351) is titled "Special Directives". Statement 2 is wrong: Article 351 directs Hindi to draw its vocabulary primarily from Sanskrit, not English.

q: Under Article 344(2) of the Constitution, the duty of the Official Language Commission is to make recommendations to the President as to:

options.A: The translation of all Central Acts into Hindi
options.B: The inspection of Central Government offices for use of Hindi
options.C: The conduct of Hindi examinations for Government employees
options.D: The progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, restrictions on the use of English, the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the form of numerals to be used

e: Article 344(2) charges the Official Language Commission with recommending on the progressive use of Hindi, restrictions on the use of English, the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the form of numerals.

q: Under Article 344 of the Constitution, in making its recommendations, the Official Language Commission shall have due regard to:

options.A: The financial resources of the Union
options.B: The views of the State Governments alone
options.C: The industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services
options.D: The recommendations of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti

e: Article 344 requires the Commission, in making recommendations, to have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and to the just claims and interests of persons belonging to non-Hindi speaking areas in public services.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted in the Constitution by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956.
2. The name "Oriya" in the Eighth Schedule was replaced by "Odia" by the Constitution (96th Amendment) Act, 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956, and the name "Oriya" in the Eighth Schedule was replaced by "Odia" by the Constitution (96th Amendment) Act, 2011.

q: Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities shall submit reports on the working of the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities to:

options.D: The Governor of the State concerned

e: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submits his reports on the working of the safeguards for linguistic minorities to the President.

q: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution is designated as:
e: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed under Article 350B is designated as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.

q: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad).

q: Which of the following languages is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
e: Kashmiri is one of the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule; English, Rajasthani and Bhojpuri do not find a place in the Schedule.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Bihar is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Bihar is a Hindi-speaking State where Hindi is the official language and is widely spoken and understood, so it is placed in Region 'A'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the National Capital Territory of Delhi is placed in:
e: Delhi, where Hindi is widely spoken and understood, is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu is placed in:
e: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu is placed in Region 'B', where Hindi is not the sole official language but is spoken and understood by a large section of the people.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Kerala is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Kerala is a non-Hindi speaking State whose official language is Malayalam, so for the purposes of the Official Language Rules it falls in Region 'C'.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Assam is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Assam is a non-Hindi speaking State with Assamese as its official language, and is therefore placed in Region 'C'.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Madhya Pradesh is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Punjab is placed in Region 'B' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Madhya Pradesh, a Hindi-speaking State, is in Region 'A', and Punjab, where Hindi is widely spoken and understood though Punjabi is the official language, is in Region 'B'.

q: Which of the following is NOT required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.D: A leave application submitted by an employee

e: Section 3(3) lists specified documents such as resolutions, general orders and contracts that must be issued in both Hindi and English; a leave application submitted by an employee is not among them.

q: The Official Language Rules, 1976 have been framed by the Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by:

options.B: Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.C: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963

e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 have been framed by the Central Government in exercise of the rule-making power conferred by Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the expression "Central Government office" includes:

options.A: An office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government
options.B: The office of a private company registered under the Companies Act
options.C: The embassy of a foreign country located in India
options.D: An office of a State Government

e: For the Official Language Rules, "Central Government office" includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government; State Government and private offices are outside the definition.

q: Under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976, a Central Government office can be notified individually in the Official Gazette when the proportion of its staff who have acquired working knowledge of Hindi reaches:
e: Under Rule 10(4), a Central Government office can be notified in the Official Gazette when 80 per cent or more of its staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.

q: The authorisation given by the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, under Article 348(2) of the Constitution for the use of Hindi in the proceedings of a High Court does NOT extend to:

options.A: The arguments of the advocates in the Court
options.B: Any judgment, decree or order passed or made by the High Court
options.C: The pleadings filed in the Court
options.D: The day-to-day proceedings of the Court

e: The authorisation under Article 348(2) covers the use of Hindi in the proceedings of a High Court, but it expressly does not extend to any judgment, decree or order passed by the Court.

q: The Official Languages Act was enacted by Parliament in the year:
e: The Official Languages Act, which provides for the languages to be used for the official purposes of the Union after the initial fifteen-year period, was enacted by Parliament in 1963.

q: In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by:

options.D: A resolution of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti

e: In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960, issued on the report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language.

q: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is NOT compulsory for a Central Government employee who has attained the age of:
e: A Central Government employee who has attained the age of 45 years is exempted from compulsory in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme.

q: A Central Government employee who passes the Pragya examination with 60% or more but less than 70% marks is entitled to a cash award of:
e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: Under the incentive scheme for passing the prescribed Hindi examinations, personal pay equal to one increment is admissible to an employee for a period of:
e: Under the incentive scheme for passing the prescribed Hindi examinations, personal pay equal to one increment is admissible for a period of 12 months.

q: The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is:
e: The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 30 words per minute.

q: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by:

options.D: The Department of Official Language directly

e: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations of the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute.

q: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) was set up in the year:
e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the apex body that lays down policy for the progressive use of Hindi, was set up in the year 1967.

q: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year:
e: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi, which conducts the training and examinations of the Hindi Teaching Scheme, was established in the year 1985.

q: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is chaired by:

options.A: The senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose
options.B: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.C: The District Magistrate of the district
options.D: The Hindi Officer of the biggest office in the town

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose, so that all offices in the town coordinate implementation.

q: The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by:

options.B: The Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari of the Zonal Railway
options.D: The General Manager of the Zonal Railway

e: The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager, who heads the Division and reviews the progressive use of Hindi in its offices.

q: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was first constituted in the year:
e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti, which advises the Ministry of Railways on matters of Official Language implementation, was first constituted in the year 1973.

q: On Indian Railways, shields and cash awards for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy are given, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, to:

options.C: Hindi authors employed in the Railways

e: On Indian Railways, shields and cash awards for excellence in Official Language implementation are given, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, to Adarsh (model) stations and Adarsh workshops.

q: Besides official members, the Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry includes:

options.C: Only officers of the Department of Official Language
options.D: Members of Parliament and non-official members nominated from among Hindi scholars and experts

e: Besides official members, the Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Ministry includes Members of Parliament and non-official members nominated from among Hindi scholars and experts.

q: The Second World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1976 at:
e: The Second World Hindi Conference was held at Port Louis (Mauritius) in the year 1976, following the First Conference at Nagpur in 1975.
